In production, this means: (1) each execution’s tool-call sequence can be fully traced; (2) code generated from identical queries can be hashed and results reused; (3) code can be committed to Git, allowing the team to review search behavior changes. pupb4k:228: Dimension: frontier models are already very good at reasoning over a fixed context, but the most powerful AI systems need to be able to steer how that context is retrieved, processed, aggregated, and rendered. Traditional search systems were not designed for this level of controllability, while modern frontier models, through code-capable agent harnesses, can already exercise fine-grained control over any computational primitive via computer code — the key task is providing the right primitives.
s5cv2u:224: The limitation of traditional function calling and MCP is that they only provide a linear call trajectory—the agent decides which tools to call, then gets results. The core reason SaC breaks through this limitation is that it gives the agent the expressive power of a full programming language, not just a limited tool palette. This means the agent can dynamically compose primitives, execute conditional branches, and access intermediate state—things that are inexpressible in the function-calling paradigm.

sxyysr:156: SaC’s core innovation is that, rather than simply putting a traditional search API into a shell or language runtime, it carefully designs an Agentic Search SDK that exposes search building blocks at the most atomic level. This allows the model to directly control each individual search step—retrieval, ranking, filtering, fan-out, rendering, etc.—while also giving the model efficient access to intermediate state (such as candidate lists and ranking signals).
y69xq3:222: Perplexity emphasizes “carefully engineered” rather than simply wrapping an existing API. This means the primitives are designed according to two principles: (1) expose search building blocks at the most atomic level, giving the model maximum control granularity; (2) each primitive has a clear input/output schema that can be flexibly composed by LLMs. This design enables agents to design custom search pipelines spanning thousands of retrieval operations, optimize these pipelines on the fly, and consume only the most useful information as model context.
